description: Issue #839 AC4, the Core half of "nothing shadows": `define first :xs … end` then `print first [10 20 30]`. Phase-1 registration raises the same `ol-reserved-word` with the same `params` at the same span as `check()`, so the two stages agree and nothing runs. The printed value is what makes this discriminating: `10` means the primitive won, `999` means the procedure won, and an empty event stream means the declaration was rejected before either could. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists, but it runs only under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — NOT in this fixture, which is checked — and when it does run it is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why the runtime's copy never appears beside the check's. So nothing here observes that copy, and reading this fixture as evidence for it would be a mistake: measured, a runtime guard can be deleted outright with the whole conformance corpus still green, because the surviving report is the check's either way. What the runtime copy uniquely contributes is that the run STOPS at the fault, which is written in the event stream rather than in the diagnostics and is pinned by `packages/runtime/src/runtime-guards-halt.test.mjs`.
